newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Violence not seen affecting Israel budget.
newsitem.headline: Violence not seen affecting Israel budget.

text.p: Israel's budget has not been affected by recent Palestinian unrest but economic growth in 1997 could be hurt if the unrest continues, Treasury sources said.

Last week's clashes between Palestinians and Israeli soldiers that killed 72 people would not require any additional outlays in the budget because there has been no need to call up Israeli army reserves, the senior Treasury sources said.
The clashes were sparked by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to open a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.

Since additional spending is not expected, the government is not considering raising taxes, the sources said. However, the recent events could hurt growth next year, particularly in the tourism sector.
The Tourism Ministry has said new reservations from abroad have come to a halt in the wake of last week's unrest.
Revenue from tourism last year totalled $3.3 billion while gross domestic product (GDP) was $86.7 billion.
The Treasury sources also said they still believe this year's budget deficit, targeted at 7.6 billion shekels, will be surpassed by 3 billion to 4 billion shekels.

This is based on data from January to September. However, if October figures indicate the deviation from the target is even greater, additional cuts -- beyond a planned 350 million shekel cut -- in 1996 may be made. The sources also said that if parliament passes the 1997 budget before the end of the year, cuts planned for 1997 may be brought forward to 1996.
